newsitem.title: GREECE: Black Sea Trade Bank to start operating in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Black Sea Trade Bank to start operating in 1997.

text.p: The Black Sea Trade and Development Bank, set up by 11 countries, is expected to start operations in January, bank officials said on Saturday.
The bank's preparatory committee met in this northern Greek port city on Thursday and Friday. The officials said another meeting was scheduled before the end of the year to finalise operating plans.
"We have agreed that the bank's administration should be handed over to its management before the end of the year," said Nikos Zahariadis, head of the preparatory committee.

He said seven of the 11 member states -- Albania, Greece, Armenia, Moldova, Romania, Russia and Turkey -- had so far ratified a 1994 agreement to set up the bank. These states make up 69 percent of the bank's equity capital.
The other four states -- Bulgaria, Georgia, Ukraine, and Ajerbaijan -- are due to ratify the agreement in the next three months.
The bank will have its headquarters in Salonika and its first president will be Ersoy Volkan of Turkey.
It will have an initial share capital of one billion dollars and its priorities include investments in former communist states.
